To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of complete binary Edwards curves with the efficient affine mapping proposed in this paper results in faster point multiplication than on ordinary elliptic curves.

(1) the affine mapping from elliptic curves to binary Edwards curves can be implemented efficiently using a single inversion and no multiplications; (2) the affine mapping has few exceptional points; (3) the resulting binary Edwards curve point operations can be implemented more efficiently than the corresponding elliptic curve point operations, in terms of both timing and code complexity; and (4) this results in a significant reduction in the cost of elliptic curve point multiplication on a large multiplier.

• The algorithm presented in this paper for computing the birational map between an elliptic curve and a binary Edwards curve, when implemented on a 512-bit hardware multiplier, is significantly more efficient than the standard implementation of point multiplication on an elliptic curve.
